title: Most-Expected Questions: Physics (Ch 9–12)
subject: Science
chapter: Light · Human Eye · Electricity · Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
instructions: These are the question types that come up again and again in board papers. Answer them in your notebook, then check with the answer key.
Numericals: given → formula → substitution (with signs) → answer with unit.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of the power of a lens?
questions.answer: Dioptre (D).

questions.q: What is the focal length of a plane mirror?
questions.answer: Infinity.

questions.q: Which spherical mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image?
questions.answer: A convex mirror.

questions.q: What is the far point of a normal human eye?
questions.answer: Infinity.

questions.q: Which phenomenon makes the clear sky look blue?
questions.answer: Scattering of light.

questions.q: Write the SI unit of resistivity.
questions.answer: Ohm metre (Ω m).

questions.q: Which has more resistance: a 100 W or a 60 W bulb (both rated 220 V)?
questions.answer: The 60 W bulb. R = V^{2}/P, so 806.7 Ω versus 484 Ω.

questions.q: What is the colour of the insulation on the earth wire?
questions.answer: Green.

questions.q: The magnification produced by a plane mirror is +1. What does this mean?
questions.answer: The image is the same size as the object (|m| = 1), and the + sign shows it is virtual and erect.

questions.q: Find the focal length of a lens of power –2.0 D. What type of lens is it?
questions.answer: f = 1/P = 1/(–2.0) = –0.5 m = –50 cm. It is a concave (diverging) lens.

questions.q: You want an erect image of an object using a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Where should the object be? Will the image be larger or smaller?
questions.answer: Between the pole and the focus, that is, less than 15 cm from the mirror. The image will be larger than the object (and virtual).

questions.q: Why are copper and aluminium wires usually used for transmitting electricity?
questions.answer: They have very low resistivity, so little energy is wasted as heat. They are also good conductors and fairly cheap (aluminium is light as well).

questions.q: How does the resistance of a wire change when (a) its length is doubled and (b) its area of cross-section is doubled?
questions.answer: (a) It doubles (R ∝ L). (b) It halves (R ∝ 1/A).

questions.q: Why does a ray of light bend when it passes from air into glass?
questions.answer: The speed of light is lower in glass (an optically denser medium) than in air. This change in speed at the boundary makes the ray bend towards the normal.

questions.q: Why is the tungsten filament of a bulb able to glow without melting? Why are bulbs filled with nitrogen or argon?
questions.answer: Tungsten has a very high melting point (3380 °C). The chemically inactive gases stop the hot filament from oxidising, so it lasts longer.

questions.q: Why is the magnetic field inside a long solenoid said to be uniform?
questions.answer: Inside the solenoid the field lines are parallel straight lines, which shows the field has the same strength and direction at all points.

questions.q: An object 4 cm high is placed 25 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position, size and nature of the image.
questions.answer: u = –25 cm, f = –15 cm. 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = –1/15 + 1/25 = –2/75, so v = –37.5 cm (in front of the mirror). m = –v/u = –(–37.5)/(–25) = –1.5, so h′ = –6 cm. The image is real, inverted and magnified (6 cm tall).

questions.q: An object is placed 12 cm in front of a convex mirror of radius of curvature 30 cm. Find the position and nature of the image.
questions.answer: f = R/2 = +15 cm, u = –12 cm. 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = 1/15 + 1/12 = 9/60, so v ≈ +6.7 cm (behind the mirror). m = –v/u ≈ +0.56. The image is virtual, erect and diminished.

questions.q: A 6 Ω and a 3 Ω resistor are joined in parallel, and this combination is connected in series with a 2 Ω and a 3 Ω resistor across a 12 V battery. Find the total resistance and the current.
An electric motor takes 5 A from a 220 V line. Find its power and the energy it uses in 2 hours.
The hot plate of an electric oven on a 220 V line has two coils A and B of 24 Ω each, which can be used separately, in series or in parallel. Find the current in each case.
questions.answer: Separately: I = 220/24 ≈ 9.2 A. In series: R = 48 Ω, I = 220/48 ≈ 4.6 A. In parallel: R = 12 Ω, I = 220/12 ≈ 18.3 A.

questions.q: A copper wire 1 km long has a cross-sectional area of 0.5 mm^{2}. Find its resistance. (ρ of copper = 1.62 × 10^{-8} Ω m)

(a) How would you connect three resistors of 6 Ω each to get a total resistance of (i) 9 Ω and (ii) 4 Ω? [3]
(b) Several 10 W bulbs are designed for a 220 V line. How many can be connected in parallel if the maximum allowed current is 5 A? [2]
questions.answer: (a) (i) Two in parallel (3 Ω), then the third in series: 3 + 6 = 9 Ω. (ii) Two in series (12 Ω), then that pair in parallel with the third: 1/R = 1/12 + 1/6 = 1/4, so R = 4 Ω. (b) Maximum power = VI = 220 × 5 = 1100 W. Number of bulbs = 1100/10 = 110.

questions.q:
(a) Draw ray diagrams for a convex lens with the object (i) at 2F_{1} and (ii) between F_{1} and O. State the nature and position of the image in each case. [3]
(b) Why does a convex lens act as a magnifying glass? [2]
questions.answer: (a) (i) The image is at 2F_{2}: real, inverted, same size. (ii) The image is on the same side as the object: virtual, erect, enlarged. Use two rays in each: one parallel to the axis that passes through F_{2}, and one through O undeviated. (b) When the object is placed between F_{1} and the optical centre, a convex lens forms a virtual, erect and enlarged image, so small things look bigger.

questions.q:
(a) What is myopia? Explain its causes and correction. [3]
(b) Why does the Sun appear reddish at sunrise and sunset? [2]
questions.answer: (a) A person with myopia can see near objects clearly but not distant ones, because the image forms in front of the retina. Causes: excessive curvature of the eye lens, or elongation of the eyeball. Correction: a concave lens of suitable power. (b) Near the horizon, sunlight travels a longer path through the atmosphere. Most of the blue light is scattered away, so mainly red light, which is scattered least, reaches our eyes.

closing: Every numerical: units first, signs second, arithmetic last!
